Subject: Log escrow & retention: mapping needed for SIG/SOC2 response

Hi Priya,

We're working through our vendor SIG and there are a couple of controls where we need a vendor-side mapping for log retention and an option for a customer-specific escrow for immutable forensic logs. Specifically:
- Our compliance group requires a 24-month immutable copy of certain forensic/access logs (authentication events, admin actions, and request-level metadata) for audit.
- We need to know which Redwood logs contain request payloads (if any), which logs contain PII, and which are configurable for longer retention.
- If Redwood can support a data-escrow for logs (stored offsite / immutable for 24 months), we'll need basic terms and a draft agreement for our procurement/security review.

Can you map the log types to Redwood's retention default and whether an escrow/exception is possible? I've attached our SIG questionnaire extract and a small spreadsheet listing the exact fields we need.

Thanks,
Alex

Thanks Priya / Alex — quick technical summary from Security: 

- Request/ingestion logs: short-lived in our runtime cache (default TTL 0–7 days for payloads). Metadata (request IDs, timestamps, routing) is persisted to our aggregated logging pipeline. Default retention for aggregated operational logs is 365 days (S3-backed, encrypted at rest).
- Audit/admin logs: these are persisted to the audit events store and retained for 365 days by default; retention can be extended for enterprise customers via Dedicated/Private deployments or a config change for an additional fee (we can push to 730 days).
- Request payloads: Redwood does not store full request payloads by default for hosted customers unless customer enables "session capture". If enabled, capture is configurable and can be persisted to a customer-controlled bucket (preferred) or Redwood-managed storage with retention settings.
- KV cache / model context: strictly ephemeral; not persisted to long-term storage.

Escrow note: traditional data-escrow for logs (immutable, offsite) is not standard but doable as an enterprise add-on. Key considerations: PII minimization (we strongly recommend redaction prior to escrow), immutability guarantees (WORM storage or third-party escrow vendor), and an agreed retention window. We'll need procurement and legal to align on SLA/indemnity and likely require a one-time setup + recurring fee.

I'll pull the relevant SOC2 control excerpts we can reference and a short mapping doc for the SIG controls you surfaced.

-Marissa

- Scope: authentication events, admin actions (role changes, permission grants), and request metadata (headers, timestamps, IPs). We do NOT need full request payloads; metadata-only is acceptable.

Alex — thanks for the clarifications. Action plan and answers below.

1) Retention mapping (by log type) — proposed:
   - Authentication events: default retention 365 days; enterprise config available up to 730 days. If MedSage opts in, we will include the authentication-event stream in the escrow export.
   - Admin/audit events: persisted 365 days by default; can extend to 730 days for enterprise. Included in escrow upon opt-in.
   - Request metadata (headers, timestamps, IPs): persisted to aggregated logs 365 days by default; config to export metadata-only (no payload) to escrow for 24 months.
   - Request payloads / model inputs: not included unless session capture is enabled by MedSage. By default, we will not include payloads in any escrow.
   - KV cache / transient context: not persisted, excluded from any export.

2) PII & redaction: Redwood will provide a redaction step in the export pipeline (simple PII tokenization — email/SSN regex) and we recommend MedSage perform downstream validation on your side prior to ingestion into your audit systems.

3) Escrow approach and commercial:
   - We can support a third-party escrow (WORM storage) for immutable retention for 24 months. Implementation requires: one-time setup (provisioning, mapping, legal agreement), monthly storage & maintenance fee. Draft escrow agreement attached (proposed-data-escrow-agreement.pdf).
   - If MedSage prefers, we can also configure an enterprise Dedicated instance and ship exports directly to a MedSage-managed bucket (recommended if you want direct possession). Dedicated/Private is a larger lift but reduces legal complexity around escrow.

4) Deliverables & timeline:
   - Marissa will attach SOC2 control excerpts and a SIG control mapping file (by EOD tomorrow).
   - Ben will produce a commercial term sheet with setup fee and monthly storage estimate (2 business days).
   - I will circulate a short export/validation technical runbook and the DocuSign link for the escrow agreement.

Next steps for MedSage: please confirm you accept metadata-only exports with Redwood-performed redaction. Once you confirm, we will prepare the DocuSign package.
